label: verify-automated-findings
name: A Cursor, Bugbot, Codex, Claude or GPT finding is traced to the initialization site, the caller or the PR's stated intent before being endorsed, refuted or forwarded
description: What breaks: a bot claim is posted without the line that proves or disproves it. Wade refutes '-1 reaches the callee' by quoting the resolving initializer (3082075451 'this is a false negative... max_layers up in llama.cpp is initialized like this:'); refutes 'unused parameter' by quoting the caller (3088359578 'wrong... this populate method is used by the model code, here:'); dismisses a finding because the flagged behavior is the PR's purpose (3659990818 'that's the point of this PR, lol'); runs his own Claude review and forwards four items as optional follow-ups with a merit judgment (4800935083 'I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up'). Endorsements after his own reading sit inside the mechanism checks (2983833171, 3002297607, 3437517809, 3463061252, 3125517302, 3307473806, 3156090573, 2948090978, 2915281512, 3970590653, 5498556672): the pattern is 'I do think there's merit to this complaint' plus the line that proves it. Procedure: for each bot or agent finding, trace the value to its initializer and every caller, compare the finding with the PR title and body, and post either the proving line or the refuting line; forwarded agent items carry a merit judgment and a severity.
disposition_reason: A procedure, not a style habit: read the init site or caller before accepting or posting a bot claim. 4 rows over 3 PRs; taxonomy 1 placed these under non-review but named the same reusable step.
agent_feasibility: yes: for each bot claim, trace the value to its initializer and callers before agreeing; compare against the PR body.

members.concern: Refutes the cursor bot's high-severity claim that passing cfg.max_layers (-1 default) to gof_configure yields a huge layer count: the config's max_layers is resolved at construction to model_t::n_layers when the command line gives -1.

detection.trigger: A bot or reviewer claims a value reaches a callee with its declared default (e.g. -1), based on the declaration alone.
detection.procedure: Grep h/ src/ for the member's initializer in the constructor initializer list or the config loader (here max_layers(is_eagle ? 1 : cfg->max_layers == -1 ? model_t::n_layers : cfg->max_layers)); check whether the object at the call site is the resolved copy or the raw command-line struct.
detection.question: At the call site, has the value already been resolved from its sentinel default by an initializer the bot did not read?

members.quote: this is a false negative... max_layers up in llama.cpp is initialized like this:
members.note: Verified at 4666560ff1: the initializer Wade quotes is at h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1060-1062, not in llama.cpp as his comment says. Whether the cfg at model.hpp:829 is that resolved copy was not traced here. Wade writes 'false negative' where he means false positive. The comment is a reply to cursor[bot], not to the author.

members.concern: Refutes the cursor bot's claim that gof::populate's new pages parameter is unused by quoting the model-code caller that passes job.gal_ptr->pages.

detection.trigger: A bot or reviewer claims a function, parameter or member is unused.
detection.procedure: grep -rn '<symbol>(' h/ src/ t/ at HEAD; list callers with file:line and the argument passed in the position the claim is about.
detection.question: Does any caller at HEAD pass the parameter or read the member the claim says is unused?

members.quote: wrong... this populate method is used by the model code, here:
members.note: Verified at 4666560ff1:h/tron/models/model.hpp:1598 'g->populate(n_kv_heads, head_size, layer, dev, job.gal_ptr->pages);'. The bot's actual point (the gof struct's own pages[] member being dead while the parameter shadows it) is not what Wade answered; he answered the 'unused parameter' reading. Reply to cursor[bot].

members.concern: Wade dismisses the Cursor Bugbot finding that the engaged `false` return makes the `default_enabled` fallthrough unreachable, because making 'unset' mean disabled is exactly the PR's purpose and USE_HW_ATTN=1 still enables hardware attention.

detection.trigger: An automated reviewer (Cursor Bugbot, Codex) posts a finding on a hunk, and the PR title or body states the behavior the bot flags as the goal of the change.
detection.procedure: Read the bot finding, the PR title and the one-time env read in the hunk (`hw_attn_env_override`: `v != nullptr` -> `atoi(v) > 0`, else `false`). Enumerate the three input states (unset, =0, =1) and the resulting value; compare with the title 'flip HW attention off by default in a way that's easy to toggle back on'. Check that the toggle-on path (=1) is unchanged. Note that the bot's 'callers still pass model_forces_hw_attn()' observation is a dead-parameter cleanup, not a defect.
detection.question: Is the behavior the bot calls a defect the behavior the PR title or body says it introduces on purpose, and does the opt-in path still work?

members.quote: that's the point of this PR, lol... 'unset' leaves it disabled, and `USE_HW_ATTN=1` still turns it on for all eligible models. Looks fine to me.
members.note: Reply to cursor[bot] on commit 2a3fb52d5a. The hunk changes `return std::nullopt;` to `return false;` in hw_attn_env_override() when USE_HW_ATTN is unset. Wade approved in the same minute (review 4790383475). He did not ask the author to remove the now-unreachable default_enabled parameter or the ingest `force_hw_attn = true` emission the bot mentioned. The PR body is 'later'; he did not ask for a body.

members.concern: He approves the PR as read, then pastes four items from a Claude review he ran (fragile copy of Perfetto internal macros with no version pin; emission sites that bypass the gating header; undocumented single-writer assumption on process-global relaxed atomics; help-text gap for per-generation pass renumbering) as optional follow-ups with 'some merit'.

detection.trigger: The PR copies or overrides a third-party library's internal macros or relies on process-global mutable state; or more generally the PR is large and Wade has read it without findings of his own.
detection.procedure: Run an agent review of the diff; for each item classify: (a) copied upstream implementation -> check for a version/commit pin in the comment and a runtime test that exercises the override (grep '#undef' + 'PERFETTO_INTERNAL' in h/common/perfetto.hpp, grep the test for an assertion that a real emitted slice is suppressed); (b) a gate implemented in one header -> grep the tree for direct includes of the upstream header that bypass it (grep -rn 'include <perfetto' h/ src/ excluding the gating header); (c) process-global atomics with relaxed ordering -> look for a comment stating the single-writer invariant; (d) documented behaviour (README) absent from `--help` text -> diff README claims against the CLI usage string.
detection.question: Which agent-review items name a real mechanism (version drift, bypass path, undocumented invariant, help/README mismatch), and are they worth a follow-up rather than a block?

members.quote: This all looked good to me when I went through it Bret. I did ask claude to do a review as well. Below are the items it came up with. I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up if you prefer.
members.note: APPROVED at 6e3f089 (commit not present in the repository, so the before state is unreadable). The branch commit list contains 'Document trace gate invariants and version pin' after this review, matching pasted items 1 (version pin) and 3 (single-writer invariant comment), hence outcome=changed (inferred from the commit subject, not from a reply). Sub-pattern slugs for the four pasted items: copied-upstream-macro-needs-version-pin, gate-bypass-via-direct-include, global-relaxed-atomic-needs-single-writer-note, help-text-lags-readme. Pattern: since 2026-07 Wade forwards agent findings verbatim in a blockquote, marks them optional and approves anyway.

codex_bullets.bullet: Reuse existing configuration accessors and model parameters instead of copying environment reads or deriving a setting from a correlated dimension. Check that the normal wrapper or entry point exposes the feature.
codex_bullets.reason: Five quoted (PRs 3016, 2089, 2426, 2176, 3490); also 3029194687, 3036995239, 2915275194, 3866435051. One of the most frequent themes in the corpus. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Separate correctness defects, coverage gaps, inaccurate claims, design questions, and nonblocking nits.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4596, 4128, 4557, 3490). Already in the Claude skill.

codex_bullets.bullet: Do not turn an approved follow-up into a blocker.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 2766, 3490, 4267, 2980, 2176). Wade approves with follow-ups often (100 of 334 reviews approved, 0 changes requested); one sentence in the Claude skill would stop an agent from escalating these.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (severity words listed; no rule about follow-ups)
